title: snapshot-backed micro-canary with instant-revert hooks and traffic reservation
author: Aisha Patel
description: Context: We frequently run very small canaries (0.1-1% traffic) for model swaps but have hit two operational issues in the past quarter: 1) slow manual revert when a micro-canary exhibits a severe regression, and 2) noisy traffic shaping during short-lived probes which causes headroom oscillation on Dedicated pools. Motivation: provide a lightweight, resumable micro-canary primitive that reserves a tiny traffic slice on a node pool, captures a compact runtime snapshot at promotion time, and exposes an instant-revert hook that can roll state back and begin replay from the snapshot with minimal disruption. This PR adds a snapshot-backed micro-canary coordinator, traffic-reservation knobs in the agent, and a simple instant-revert API that replays buffered requests against the snapshot in a quarantined lane for verification before release. Design highlights: - Traffic reservation: a soft reservation token is requested from the node allocator when a micro-canary starts; reservation enforces an upper bound on burst capacity and prevents autoscaler churning for the duration of the probe. - Snapshot capture: when the micro-canary reaches the configured warmup window, we capture a compressed KV snapshot (metadata + trimmed tokenized cache) and persist to the PromotedSnapshots store (TTL 24h). - Instant revert hook: if rollback is triggered (manual or automated policy), controller triggers the instant-revert sequence: 1) mark canary lane draining; 2) instantiate a quarantined replay plane keyed to the snapshot id; 3) replay buffered requests for 30s (configurable) and compare deterministic checksums/observations; 4) if replay checks pass, promote snapshot to candidate for controlled backfill; otherwise keep original model or escalate. - Resumability: micro-canary state (progress markers, reservation id, snapshot id) is persisted so interrupted canaries can resume without re-probing full warmup. - Telemetry and safety: adds per-canary metrics (reserved_tokens, snapshot_size_bytes, replay_pass_ratio), a canary-level health timeline for the Console, and new alert rules (canary-replay-failure, reservation-starve). Implementation notes: - rollout/controller/mini_canary_coordinator.go: new coordinator with a compact state machine (INIT -> RESERVE -> WARMUP -> SNAPSHOT -> VERIFY -> PROMOTE/REVERT -> COMPLETE). - agent/pool_allocator/reservation.go: reservation token APIs and soft quotas. - runtime/snapshotter: lightweight snapshot format (protobuf) + compression. - api/rollback/v1: instant-revert endpoints (POST /canaries/:id/revert, GET /canaries/:id/snapshots). - docs/runbooks/micro-canary.md: operator runbook, migration notes and troubleshooting. Backwards compatibility: micro-canary is an opt-in rollout mode (canary.mode: "micro-snapshot") and defaults to off; existing canary behavior unchanged. Test plan: - Unit tests for coordinator state transitions and reservation logic (coverage added). - Integration test that runs a simulated micro-canary against the local allocator (flaky test fixed). - E2E smoke including snapshot persistence and replay verification against fuzzed inputs. - Manual pre-merge verification: exercised on staging Dedicated pool with a synthetic model and a 0.5% traffic slice. Rollout plan: 1) merge to main behind feature flag rollout.nonblocking.micro_canary; 2) enable in staging for 48h; 3) enable opt-in in a single low-traffic customer in Dedicated (platform team will coordinate); 4) expand to canary customers after two successful cycles. Observability and runbook: Console exposes a new per-canary timeline view and replay diff artifacts; runbook covers immediate manual revert steps and diagnosing reservation contention. Related work: builds on prior snapshotting design from ENG-2192 and the reservation API introduced in ENG-2899. Links: Linear ENG-3421 for feature scope, ENG-4278 for monitoring SLOs, internal doc: https://linear.redwood.internal/ENG-3421. Security notes: snapshot payloads are encrypted at rest with tenant KMS; snapshots include only compact model runtime metadata and trimmed token cache (no raw prompt payloads). Open questions: - Should snapshot TTL be configurable per-tenant? (proposal: yes, default 24h). - We currently replay for 30s by default; ops wanted a replay window metric to drive later autoscaling. CI: one flaky integration test flaked on first run due to test fixture timing; rerun passed. This PR also updates docs and adds a runbook and a small console backend change for a timeline endpoint.

review_comments: Miguel Ortega: Can we avoid persisting the entire KV cache for the snapshot? Suggest trimming to hot prefixes only.
Aisha Patel (author): Answered: snapshotter now trims to hot prefixes and we gzip; added unit test to verify size reduction.
Hannah Liu: What happens if reservation tokens cannot be granted due to high contention? Which pool fallback path is used?
Aisha Patel (author): We fall back to 'best-effort' probe without reservation and mark canary as degraded; added metric reservation_starve_count and doc section.
Jonah Weiss: Add a smoke test that asserts instant revert completes within 5s under synthetic load?
Aisha Patel (author): Added an e2e harness check that measures revert latency; currently median ~2.3s in staging under synthetic load.
Miguel Ortega: CI integ flake - thanks for stabilizing the fixture. APPROVED after tests passed.
Hannah Liu: Left a minor doc nit; otherwise LGTM.
release_notes:
- Add opt-in 'micro-snapshot' canary mode: supports snapshot-backed micro-canaries with traffic reservation and instant-revert hooks.
- Adds reservation tokens to allocator, snapshot store and replay verification.
- New Console timeline view and operator runbook for micro-canaries.
additional_notes: This is intentionally gated by rollout.nonblocking.micro_canary. Platform will coordinate a small Dedicated customer pilot before broad rollout. Operator training session scheduled for 2026-03-03.
